title.es: Detectar los fallos de un borrador

es: Leer un borrador y localizar repeticiones, referencias ambiguas, saltos lógicos, frases irrelevantes y contradicciones, nombrando cada problema.

vocabulary.es: non sequitur, conclusión que no se deduce
antecedente (a lo que remite un pronombre)

teaching.en: A rough draft is often repetitive: the same noun opens every sentence, and the reader hears an echo instead of an argument.
teaching.es: Un borrador suele ser repetitivo: el mismo sustantivo abre cada frase, y el lector oye un eco en lugar de un argumento.
teaching.explanationEs: Repetitive describe un texto que insiste con las mismas palabras.
segments: A rough draft is often repetitive: the same noun opens every
sentence, and the reader hears an echo instead of an argument.
teaching.audioText: A rough draft is often repetitive: the same noun opens every sentence, and the reader hears an echo instead of an argument.

teaching.en: In the sentence Ana told Mia that she was late, the pronoun is ambiguous, since its antecedent could be either girl.
teaching.es: En la frase «Ana le dijo a Mia que ella llegaba tarde», el pronombre es ambiguo, pues su antecedente podría ser cualquiera de las dos.
teaching.explanationEs: El antecedente es la palabra a la que remite un pronombre.
segments: In the sentence Ana told Mia that she was late, the
pronoun is ambiguous, since its antecedent could be either girl.
teaching.audioText: In the sentence Ana told Mia that she was late, the pronoun is ambiguous, since its antecedent could be either girl.

teaching.en: A writer who jumps to a conclusion leaves a logical gap, so the reader stays unclear about the reasoning.
teaching.es: Un autor que saca conclusiones precipitadas deja un salto lógico, y el lector sigue sin tener claro el razonamiento.
teaching.explanationEs: Jumps to a conclusion = concluye sin pasos intermedios.
segments: A writer who jumps to a conclusion leaves a logical
gap, so the reader stays unclear about the reasoning.
teaching.audioText: A writer who jumps to a conclusion leaves a logical gap, so the reader stays unclear about the reasoning.

teaching.en: A paragraph on school buses should not go off on a tangent about holidays, because an irrelevant sentence weakens the point.
teaching.es: Un párrafo sobre autobuses escolares no debería irse por las ramas hablando de vacaciones, porque una frase irrelevante debilita la idea.
teaching.explanationEs: Irrelevant = no tiene que ver con el tema del párrafo.
segments: A paragraph on school buses should not go off on a
tangent about holidays, because an irrelevant sentence weakens the point.
teaching.audioText: A paragraph on school buses should not go off on a tangent about holidays, because an irrelevant sentence weakens the point.

teaching.en: When one sentence contradicts another, the paragraph collapses, and a non sequitur, which follows from nothing, does the same damage.
teaching.es: Cuando una frase contradice a otra, el párrafo se viene abajo, y un non sequitur, que no se deduce de nada, hace el mismo daño.
teaching.explanationEs: Contradicts lleva objeto directo: contradicts the first sentence, sin to.
segments: When one sentence contradicts another, the paragraph collapses, and a
non sequitur, which follows from nothing, does the same damage.
teaching.audioText: When one sentence contradicts another, the paragraph collapses, and a non sequitur, which follows from nothing, does the same damage.

teaching.en: Vague wording such as things or stuff leaves the reader unclear about the point, so replace it with the exact noun.
teaching.es: Una redacción vaga, con palabras como «cosas», deja al lector sin tener claro el punto, así que sustitúyela por el sustantivo exacto.
teaching.explanationEs: Vague wording = palabras demasiado generales; se opone a precise.
segments: Vague wording such as things or stuff leaves the reader unclear
about the point, so replace it with the exact noun.
teaching.audioText: Vague wording such as things or stuff leaves the reader unclear about the point, so replace it with the exact noun.

prompt.es: ¿Qué problema principal tiene este fragmento del borrador?

choices.text: It is repetitive: the same noun opens every sentence.
It is ambiguous: each pronoun could refer to two things.
It contradicts itself about the size of the town.

feedback.es: Las tres frases empiezan por «The town» y no aportan una progresión: el problema es la repetición.

origin.text: The town is small. The town has a river. The town has a market. The town has a school.

prompt.es: Completa: «Palabras como «cosas» son vagas: no dan nada concreto que imaginar.»

feedback.es: Vague describe una palabra demasiado general; la solución es sustituirla por el sustantivo exacto.

hint.es: Adjetivo que se opone a specific.

origin.text: Words such as things and stuff are ___, because they give readers nothing exact to picture. A precise noun is always better.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La segunda frase contradice directamente a la primera.»

answer.text: The second sentence directly contradicts the first one

feedback.es: Contradicts es transitivo: va seguido de the first one, sin preposición.

hint.es: Directly va justo antes del verbo contradicts.

prompt.es: Identifica el problema principal del párrafo.

choices.text: It is ambiguous: the pronouns could refer to two different things.
It contradicts itself about how many members the club has.
It jumps to a conclusion that the figures do not support.
It is repetitive: almost every sentence opens with the same words.

feedback.es: «The club» abre casi todas las frases y el párrafo suena a eco: el fallo es la repetición.

origin.text: The club needs a new room. The club has three hundred members. The club's members want a room. The club's room is too small, so the club must find another room for the club's members.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué solución propone la editora.

choices.text: Replace the pronoun with the noun it stands for.
Delete the sentence because it is irrelevant to the report.
Add a figure to support the claim about the promotion.
Change the verb to a stronger one that the reader remembers.

feedback.es: La editora propone repetir el sustantivo para eliminar la duda sobre a quién remite «he».

origin.audio: A student wrote: The manager told the assistant that he would be promoted. I asked him who would be promoted, and he did not know either. The pronoun he has two possible antecedents, the manager and the assistant, and the reader cannot decide. I suggested repeating the noun. It is a small change, but it removes the doubt completely.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada fragmento con el problema que presenta.

pairs: Ana told Mia she was late.
It is cheap. It costs a lot.
A holiday in a report on buses.

feedback.es: Cada fragmento ilustra un fallo distinto: salto, ambigüedad, contradicción e irrelevancia.

pairs: Ana told Mia she was late.
It is cheap. It costs a lot.
A holiday in a report on buses.

prompt.es: ¿Qué problema presenta la frase 4 del borrador?

choices.text: It is repetitive, because it says the same thing about the route twice.
It contradicts itself, because a free route cannot charge two pounds a journey.
It is irrelevant, because fares have nothing to do with a route.
It is ambiguous, because the pronoun could refer to two different stages.

feedback.es: La frase afirma que la ruta será gratuita para los alumnos y a la vez que cada alumno debe pagar dos libras por trayecto: una contradicción interna.

origin.text: (1) The school plan for the new bus route is a good plan. (2) The plan was written by the council, and the plan has three stages. (3) Ana told Mia she had to submit it before Friday. (4) The route will be free for pupils, but every pupil must pay two pounds for each journey. (5) My holiday in Spain was wonderful. (6) As a result, the plan is sure to be a success, although no pupil has tried the new route yet. The draft was sent to the head teacher on Monday, together with a short note from the council explaining that the plan would start in September if the pupils agreed.

prompt.es: ¿Qué deja entrever la frase 6 sobre el razonamiento del autor?

choices.text: That it contradicts the claim that the route will be free.
That it repeats the idea of the first sentence in other words.
That it reaches a conclusion the earlier sentences do not justify.
That it uses a pronoun whose antecedent cannot be identified.

feedback.es: La frase concluye que el plan será un éxito aunque nadie ha probado la ruta: es un salto lógico sin apoyo en lo anterior.

origin.text: (1) The school plan for the new bus route is a good plan. (2) The plan was written by the council, and the plan has three stages. (3) Ana told Mia she had to submit it before Friday. (4) The route will be free for pupils, but every pupil must pay two pounds for each journey. (5) My holiday in Spain was wonderful. (6) As a result, the plan is sure to be a success, although no pupil has tried the new route yet. The draft was sent to the head teacher on Monday, together with a short note from the council explaining that the plan would start in September if the pupils agreed.

prompt.es: Completa: «El pronombre es ambiguo porque puede referirse a cualquiera de las dos.»

feedback.es: Un pronombre con dos antecedentes posibles es ambiguous: el lector no puede decidir a quién remite.

origin.text: In the sentence Sara told Luna that she had won, the pronoun is ___, because it could refer to either girl.

prompt.es: Escribe una nota de edición para la frase 5: nombra el problema y explica por qué.

answer.text: This sentence is irrelevant, because a holiday in Spain has nothing to do with a school bus route.
accepted: This sentence is irrelevant, because a holiday in Spain has nothing to do with a school bus route.
This sentence is off the topic, since a holiday in Spain does not belong in a report on school buses.
The sentence is irrelevant because a holiday in Spain has no connection with the bus route.

feedback.es: Una buena nota de edición nombra el problema (irrelevant) y da una razón concreta con because.

origin.text: Frase del borrador, en un informe sobre transporte escolar: «My holiday in Spain was wonderful.» Escribe en inglés una nota breve: nombra el problema y explica la razón con because.

prompt.es: ¿Qué crítica hace el editor del tercer párrafo?

choices.text: It repeats one noun until the reader hears only an echo.
It contradicts what the second paragraph said about attendance.
It relies on vague words in place of the exact nouns.
It leaves a logical gap between falling attendance and the timetable's failure.

feedback.es: El editor señala que se pasa de «attendance fell» a «the new timetable is a disaster» sin explicar la conexión: falta un paso lógico.

origin.audio: Dear Leo, I read your draft twice. Paragraph two is strong, but in the third you move from attendance fell in March to the new timetable is a disaster without explaining why the two are connected, and the final one goes off on a tangent about your holiday. I would keep the facts and add the missing step. Best wishes, Mar.

prompt.es: Completa: «Un párrafo sobre vacaciones en un informe de autobuses se irá por las ramas.»

feedback.es: Go off on a tangent significa alejarse del tema principal, como haría un párrafo sobre vacaciones en un informe de autobuses.

origin.text: The report is about school buses. A paragraph about holidays would ___ off on a tangent, and the reader would lose the thread.

prompt.es: Ordena: «El autor saca una conclusión precipitada sin ninguna prueba.»

answer.text: The writer jumps to a conclusion without any evidence
accepted: The writer jumps to a conclusion without any evidence
Without any evidence the writer jumps to a conclusion

feedback.es: Jumps to a conclusion describe concluir sin pasos intermedios; without any evidence añade la falta de pruebas.
